articles.title: India Retain Asian Games Women's Cricket Gold With Record 147-Run Win Over Sri Lanka
articles.excerpt: Smriti Mandhana's 45-ball 79 — and a record 216 for 3 — powered India to a crushing 147-run victory over Sri Lanka in the final, the country's first gold of the 2026 Asian Games.
articles.image_caption: An India batter plays a shot during the women's cricket final against Sri Lanka at the Aichi-Nagoya Asian Games. India won the final by 147 runs to retain the gold medal, the country's first gold of the 2026 Games.
articles.nri_angle: A second straight Asian Games gold — and India's first medal of the 2026 Games — gives the global Indian diaspora a marquee win to rally around, with Mandhana's record 11,000 international runs adding a historic individual milestone.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India Thrash Korea 63-31 to Stay Unbeaten at Asian Games
articles.excerpt: A day after routing hosts Japan, India's kabaddi men dominated South Korea 63–31 in Nagoya to make it two wins from two in their title defence at the 2026 Asian Games.
articles.image_caption: Action from the India vs South Korea men's kabaddi match at the 2026 Asian Games. India won 63-31 at the Tokai Citizens Gymnasium in Nagoya on September 22 to stay unbeaten in Group A.
articles.nri_angle: Kabaddi is India's indigenous sport, and the men's ruthless title defence at the Asian Games — watched by a global diaspora — is one of the purest Indian success stories on the continental stage.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India Face Japan in Historic First-Ever T20I at Sano
articles.excerpt: World No. 1 India warm up for the Asian Games against 41st-ranked Japan in a first-ever men's T20I at Sano, branded the Suzuki Cup — after rain washed out India's practice session and with no reserve day available.
articles.image_caption: Indian players celebrate during a T20 International. The reigning T20 World Cup champions face Japan in a first-ever men's T20I at the Sano International Cricket Ground on Tuesday 22 September, branded the Suzuki Cup.
articles.nri_angle: For the Indian diaspora in Japan — one of Asia's fastest-growing Indian communities — Tuesday's match is a rare homecoming of Indian cricket on Japanese soil, while fans in India get a morning fixture that doubles as a cultural bridge between two partner nations.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India Chases Cricket Gold as Sindhu Leads Packed Asian Games Day 4 Schedule
articles.excerpt: Harmanpreet Kaur's women face Sri Lanka for T20 gold at 10:30 AM IST on September 22, while PV Sindhu's badminton squad meets hosts Japan and shooters Parth Mane and Elavenil Valarivan target a medal.
articles.image_caption: PV Sindhu at a felicitation ceremony after her Olympic silver medal. Sindhu faces Japan in her Asian Games 2026 badminton tie on September 22.
articles.nri_angle: Indian fans in Japan and streaming worldwide get their first full day of medal action, with the cricket final at a diaspora-friendly mid-morning IST slot.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Chennai Super Kings Name Zaheer Khan Head Coach for IPL 2027
articles.excerpt: The five-time IPL champions ended Stephen Fleming's 16-year coaching era, handing former India pacer Zaheer Khan his first head-coach role on a one-year contract.
articles.image_caption: Zaheer Khan at a public event in Mumbai. The former India pacer has been named head coach of Chennai Super Kings for IPL 2027, succeeding Stephen Fleming after 16 years.
articles.nri_angle: CSK's enormous diaspora fanbase gets a new era to follow, with the franchise's US-based Texas Super Kings still searching for a coach of its own.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India Women Face Sri Lanka for Gold in Asian Games Cricket Final
articles.excerpt: Harmanpreet Kaur's defending champions meet Sri Lanka for the Asian Games women's cricket gold at 10:30 AM IST on September 22, while boxer Sakshi Chaudhary opens against an Olympic medallist.
articles.image_caption: Members of the Indian women's cricket team during a match at the Asian Games. India faces Sri Lanka in the women's gold medal match on September 22 at Aichi-Nagoya.
articles.nri_angle: For Indian-Americans, the women's cricket final airs at a convenient 10:00 PM PDT on Monday, September 21, and stars like Harmanpreet Kaur and Smriti Mandhana draw heavy diaspora viewership.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Suchika Tariyal Wins Historic Bronze as MMA Debuts at Asian Games
articles.excerpt: The 36-year-old lost a disputed overtime semifinal to Singapore's Teo Hui Hoon but leaves Aichi-Nagoya with India's first Asian Games medal in mixed martial arts.
articles.image_caption: Suchika Tariyal holds the Indian flag aloft after her Brave CF 92 debut victory in December 2024. The 36-year-old won bronze in the women's traditional -60kg event at the Aichi-Nagoya Asian Games on Monday, India's first-ever MMA medal at the Games.
articles.nri_angle: India's first Asian Games MMA medal arrives as the sport surges in global popularity, giving diaspora fight fans a homegrown name to follow on the international circuit.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Praggnanandhaa Downs Giri as India Beat Netherlands at Chess Olympiad
articles.excerpt: R Praggnanandhaa declined a draw offer from Anish Giri and ground out his first win in Samarkand as the defending champions beat the Netherlands 3-1 — but India's top-seeded women lost 1.5-2.5 to Poland for the third straight Olympiad.
articles.image_caption: R Praggnanandhaa defeated Anish Giri as India beat the Netherlands at the Chess Olympiad.
articles.nri_angle: The Rameshbabu siblings starred for India on opposite ends of a mixed day, and the top-board win came against Dutch No. 1 Anish Giri, born to a Nepali father in Russia.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India Rout Japan 49-24 to Open Kabaddi Title Defence at Asian Games
articles.excerpt: Ashu Malik's three-point Super Raid set the tone as debutants starred in a dominant opening group-stage win at Nagoya's Tokai Citizens Gymnasium.
articles.image_caption: India's men's kabaddi team poses for a group photograph on the mat in their blue India jerseys. The defending champions opened their Asian Games 2026 title defence with a 49-24 win over hosts Japan in Nagoya.
articles.nri_angle: Kabaddi's Pro Kabaddi League has built a growing US fanbase; India's title defence gives diaspora viewers a team to follow through the Asian Games.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Asian Games 2026: India Joint 10th After Day 1 as China, Japan Lead
articles.excerpt: India opened its Aichi-Nagoya Asian Games medal account with two shooting silvers from Elavenil Valarivan, while China and hosts Japan set the early pace with 20 medals each.
articles.image_caption: The Asian Games 2026 medal standings graphic from Aichi-Nagoya, Japan. India ended Day 1 joint 10th after winning two shooting silvers.
articles.nri_angle: For Indian fans watching from the United States and elsewhere abroad, the medal table is the daily scoreboard that matters most — Day 1's joint-10th place is a starting point, with athletics, wrestling and boxing still to come.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Umesh Yadav Parts Ways With Vidarbha, Takes NOC to Play for Another State
articles.excerpt: The 38-year-old pacer told The Indian Express the Vidarbha Cricket Association gave him no clarity on his future, prompting his departure ahead of the 2026-27 Ranji Trophy season.
articles.image_caption: Umesh Yadav celebrates a wicket with his teammates during a match. Yadav has secured an NOC from the Vidarbha Cricket Association and will represent another state from this season.
articles.nri_angle: Umesh Yadav's journey from Nagpur's streets to 170 Test wickets without formal academy training has long inspired diaspora cricket communities, and his refusal to quit at 38 keeps that story alive for young fast bowlers abroad.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Mandhana tops women's T20I run charts as India crush Bangladesh to reach Asian Games final
articles.excerpt: Smriti Mandhana passed Suzie Bates with a 19-ball 37 in the Asian Games semifinal, while Shafali Verma's unbeaten 49-ball century powered India to a 114-run win and a gold-medal clash with Sri Lanka.
articles.image_caption: Smriti Mandhana. She topped the women's T20I run charts as India beat Bangladesh to reach the Asian Games final.
articles.nri_angle: Mandhana's records travel: she sits atop every all-time women's T20I chart diaspora kids will find first, a readymade role model as women's cricket fights for visibility abroad.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: China Dominates Asian Games Swimming Opener; India Chases First Medal
articles.excerpt: China won six of seven golds on the first night of pool swimming at the 20th Asian Games in Nagoya, while India's 12-member men's squad began its campaign in the 100m freestyle and 100m backstroke heats.
articles.image_caption: Starting blocks and lane ropes at an Olympic-size swimming pool. China dominated the opening day of swimming at the 2026 Asian Games while India chased its first medal of the meet.
articles.nri_angle: For the Indian diaspora, the swimming programme is available live on the Sony Sports Network in India and through Willow TV's free Asian Games coverage in North America.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Silver in Women's 10m Air Rifle Opens India's Asian Games Account
articles.excerpt: Elavenil Valarivan, Sonam Maskar and Vidarsa Vinod finished second behind a world-record China on Day 1 at Aichi-Nagoya, while Suchika Tariyal assured India of its first-ever Asian Games MMA medal.
articles.image_caption: Elavenil Valarivan, Sonam Uttam Maskar and Vidarsa K Vinod won silver in the women's 10m air rifle team event at the Aichi-Nagoya Asian Games, India's first medal of the Games.
articles.nri_angle: No natural diaspora angle - Indian athletes competing at an international multi-sport event.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India's New-Generation Kabaddi Squad Begins Asian Games Title Defence
articles.excerpt: Debutant raider Devank Dalal headlines a refreshed Indian kabaddi contingent opening its Aichi-Nagoya campaign against hosts Japan on September 21, with both the men's and women's teams defending their 2022 golds.
articles.image_caption: India's new-generation kabaddi squad begins its Asian Games title defence at Aichi-Nagoya.
articles.nri_angle: No natural diaspora angle - kabaddi at the Asian Games is a subcontinental sporting story.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India Battle Complacency as Bangladesh Stand Between Them and Asian Games Final
articles.excerpt: Defending champions India face Bangladesh in Sunday's women's semifinal at Nisshin with a gold-medal match berth — and an unblemished Asian Games knockout record — on the line.
articles.image_caption: India's players celebrate during the women's cricket competition at the 2026 Asian Games. The defending champions face Bangladesh in the semifinal at Korogi Sports Park, Nisshin, on Sunday.
articles.nri_angle: Cricket's Asian Games return gives the small but growing Indian diaspora in Japan a rare chance to watch the women's side chase back-to-back golds on Japanese soil.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Ireland Stun Reigning World Champions India With Historic 2-0 T20I Sweep
articles.excerpt: Three months after lifting the T20 World Cup, Shreyas Iyer's new-look India were humbled at Stormont as Rajasthan-born debutant Jai Moondra inspired Ireland to their first series win over India in any format.
articles.image_caption: India's players celebrate with the trophy after winning the 2026 ICC Men's T20 World Cup final against New Zealand at the Narendra Modi Stadium in Ahmedabad. Three months later, the world champions were swept 2-0 by Ireland at Belfast.
articles.nri_angle: Jai Moondra, born in Tonk, Rajasthan and a former Intel engineer, starred for Ireland against his birth country — a storyline that resonated with the Indian diaspora in Ireland and fans back home.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Ajit Agarkar to Exit as India's Chief Selector After Defining Three Years
articles.excerpt: The 48-year-old has told the BCCI he will not seek an extension when his contract ends on October 4, ending a tenure that delivered two T20 World Cups, the Champions Trophy and some of Indian cricket's boldest selection calls.
articles.image_caption: Ajit Agarkar, chairman of the BCCI senior men's selection committee. He has informed the board he will not seek an extension when his contract ends on October 4, 2026.
articles.nri_angle: Diaspora fans who fill stadiums on India's overseas tours have a direct stake in who picks the next generation of the national team, as the new chief selector will shape the squad through the 2027 World Cup cycle.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Kamil Pooran Earns Maiden T20I Call-Up for West Indies' India Tour
articles.excerpt: The 30-year-old opener's breakout CPL 2026 season earned him a place in the T20I squad, while Jason Holder is rested and Shimron Hetmyer will join only for the T20Is.
articles.nri_angle: Indian cricket fans get a first look at Kamil Pooran and West Indies' next generation during a full white-ball tour of India starting September 27.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: IPL 2027 Auction Set for Second Week of December as BCCI Hunts for India Venue
articles.excerpt: The final mini-auction of the 2023-27 cycle returns to home soil after three years abroad — but the host city hinges on five-star hotel availability in wedding season.
articles.nri_angle: For the cricket-obsessed diaspora, the auction's return to India after three years abroad means the winter bidding spectacle happens in home time zones — and signals the BCCI's confidence ahead of the league's landmark 20th season.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Nineteen Years Later, Yuvraj's Six Sixes Still Define T20 Cricket
articles.excerpt: On September 19, 2007, an angry Yuvraj Singh took Stuart Broad apart at Kingsmead — and gave a young format its signature moment.
articles.image_caption: Yuvraj Singh. Nineteen years on, his six sixes off Stuart Broad in the 2007 T20 World Cup still define the format.
articles.nri_angle: A shared cultural timestamp for diaspora fans worldwide — everyone remembers where they were when the sixth ball cleared long-on.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Gambhir Sets 'Mission 300' After India's Afghanistan T20I Rout
articles.excerpt: India's head coach says the team's first 100-run powerplay of his tenure matters more than Abhishek Sharma's century — and 300 is the next target.
articles.image_caption: India head coach Gautam Gambhir with his players after the T20I rout of Afghanistan. He has set Mission 300 — a first-ever 300-run T20 innings — as Team India’s next target.
articles.nri_angle: Diaspora fans get the most entertaining Team India in memory — a champion side treating every game as a record-hunting mission.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Neeraj Chopra Backs Team India as Asian Games Open in Aichi-Nagoya
articles.excerpt: The Olympic champion, sidelined by an ankle ligament tear, took to X as the 20th Asian Games opened in Japan, expressing confidence the 500-strong Indian contingent would make the country proud.
articles.image_caption: Neeraj Chopra raises his arm during a javelin competition. The two-time Asian Games gold medallist will miss the 2026 Games in Aichi-Nagoya after an ankle ligament tear ended his season.
articles.nri_angle: For the Indian diaspora, Neeraj Chopra's message from the sidelines turns an injury-enforced absence into a rallying moment for the 500-strong contingent they will follow across time zones through October 4.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: BCCI Pays ₹3,000 Crore in Annual Tax, Saikia Discloses at AGM
articles.excerpt: BCCI secretary Devajit Saikia disclosed the board's income-tax outgo at the 95th Annual General Meeting, pushing back on perceptions of tax exemption as the Supreme Court seeks clarity on its status under the National Sports Governance Act.
articles.image_caption: BCCI secretary Devajit Saikia at a board press conference. Saikia disclosed at the BCCI's 95th Annual General Meeting that the board pays about INR 3,000 crore in income tax each year (Wikimedia Commons).
articles.nri_angle: For the diaspora, the BCCI's ₹3,000-crore annual tax bill underscores the scale of the cricket economy whose matches, media rights and IPL seasons fill the evenings of millions of Indian households abroad.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Shree Charani and Shafali Verma Power India Into Asian Games Cricket Semifinal
articles.excerpt: India chased 58 in five overs to beat Japan by eight wickets in Nisshin, setting up a Sunday semifinal with Bangladesh, while the mixed doubles teqball pair reached the bronze-medal match.
articles.image_caption: Shafali Verma and Shree Charani starred as India crushed Japan in the Asian Games women’s T20 quarter-final at Nisshin. Charani took 4 for 10 and Shafali hit 40 not out off 15 balls as India reached the semifinal with an eight-wicket win.
articles.nri_angle: India’s Asian Games title defence in Nagoya is a headline story for the global Indian diaspora, from fans in Japan to the large Indian communities in the US following the Games.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Aaryavir Sehwag Debuts, Anvay Dravid Fires as India U-19 Edge Australia by Seven Runs
articles.excerpt: Yashvardhan Chauhan's 54 and 2 for 28 led the way, with debutant Aaryavir Sehwag (28) and Anvay Dravid (38 off 18) starring in a rain-shortened first Youth ODI against Australia at the Niranjan Shah Stadium in Rajkot.
articles.image_caption: India's U-19 cricketers are pictured in this KhelNow photograph. Aaryavir Sehwag and Anvay Dravid starred as India beat Australia by seven runs in Rajkot.
articles.nri_angle: For NRI families, watching the sons of Virender Sehwag and Rahul Dravid play for India U-19 collapses two decades of cricket nostalgia into one game, while youth cricket remains the route many diaspora parents use to pull their children into the sport.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Indian Women Boxers Chase First Asian Games Gold Since Mary Kom's 2014 Win
articles.excerpt: An 11-member squad led by Lovlina Borgohain heads to Nagoya with momentum from Glasgow and a dominant Asian Championships — and a 12-year gold drought to end.
articles.image_caption: An Indian woman boxer competes at the Paris 2024 Olympics. India's women's team heads to the Nagoya Asian Games chasing the country's first boxing gold since Mary Kom's 2014 triumph.
articles.nri_angle: Indian boxing's new generation chases a 12-year Asian Games gold drought, carrying the legacy of Mary Kom for fans in India and the diaspora.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Typhoon Dujuan Threatens Asian Games as Nagoya Braces for Opening Weekend
articles.excerpt: Tropical storm Dujuan is tracking toward Japan's Pacific coast with gusts up to 126 kph, forcing organisers to ready contingency plans — days after record rain forced athletes to evacuate their accommodation.
articles.image_caption: Satellite view of tropical storm Dujuan off Japan's Pacific coast on September 17, 2026. Forecasters warned it could strengthen into a typhoon and reach the Aichi-Nagoya coast around September 21, threatening the opening days of the Asian Games.
articles.nri_angle: India's athletes face schedule disruption and accommodation risk at the Nagoya Games, where the contingent arrived with real medal expectations across boxing, wrestling and cricket.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India Women Open Asian Games Title Defence Against Japan in Cricket Quarter-Final
articles.excerpt: Harmanpreet Kaur's defending champions face hosts Japan in the first-ever women's T20I between the sides, with the winner advancing to Saturday's semi-final against Bangladesh.
articles.image_caption: Shafali Verma bats for India. Defending champions India opened their Asian Games 2026 women's cricket title defence against hosts Japan at Korogi Athletic Park in Nisshin.
articles.nri_angle: Cricket's global moment — a World Cup nation facing an Associate host at a multi-sport Games — is exactly the kind of fixture that plays to diaspora audiences across time zones, with free DD Sports coverage and SonyLIV streaming.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Why India May Accept Asian Games Medals From Mohsin Naqvi After Asia Cup Snub
articles.excerpt: At the Aichi-Nagoya Asian Games, the medal protocol belongs to the OCA — and its Rule 66 bans podium demonstrations, meaning Indian cricketers are expected to accept medals from whoever is delegated, even ACC chief Mohsin Naqvi.
articles.image_caption: The Indian women's cricket team poses for a group photograph after winning the Women's Asia Cup 2026 final in Dubai. India twice refused to receive Asia Cup trophies from ACC chief Mohsin Naqvi, a protocol question that now moves to the Asian Games.
articles.nri_angle: For the diaspora, the protocol question crystallises the tension between national sentiment and sporting discipline: the same fans who cheered the trophy snub in Dubai will be watching closely to see how Indian cricketers handle a podium where the rules leave them no room to refuse.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Manu Bhaker and Tajinderpal Singh Toor to Carry India's Flag at Asian Games
articles.excerpt: Double Olympic medallist Manu Bhaker and two-time Asian Games shot put champion Tajinderpal Singh Toor will lead the Indian contingent into the Paloma Mizuho Stadium on September 19 as India aims to surpass its record Hangzhou medal haul.
articles.image_caption: Shooter Manu Bhaker (left) and shot putter Tajinderpal Singh Toor. The two champions will carry the Indian flag at the opening ceremony of the Aichi-Nagoya Asian Games on September 19, 2026.
articles.nri_angle: For the Indian diaspora, the flag-bearers are the familiar face of the contingent — Bhaker's Paris heroics made her a household name in Indian homes worldwide, and her walk into the Nagoya stadium will be one of the most-watched moments of the opening ceremony.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Why Japan's Cricket Moment Signals the Game's Global Ambition
articles.excerpt: Cricket's arrival in Japan — the Asian Games plus a historic first senior men's T20I against India on September 22 — is a deliberate bet on taking the game beyond its traditional markets, and the broadcast money is following.
articles.image_caption: India's men's T20I team, the reigning world champions, walk off the field. The side will face Japan for the first time in a senior men's T20I on September 22, 2026, ahead of the Asian Games cricket tournament.
articles.nri_angle: For the Indian diaspora, Japan is the new front row — the Indian community in Japan gets a rare live sighting of the world champions, while the diaspora's global streaming audience is the commercial engine that makes a fixture like this worth broadcasting.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India Open Asian Games Cricket Title Defence Against Hosts Japan
articles.excerpt: Defending champions India face hosts Japan in the women's T20 quarter-final on September 18, opening the bid to retain both the men's and women's cricket gold at the Aichi-Nagoya Asian Games.
articles.image_caption: An India women's cricket player smiles on the field during a match. India open their Asian Games 2026 title defence against hosts Japan in the women's T20 quarter-final on September 18.
articles.nri_angle: Cricket at a continental multi-sport event gives Japan's small but growing cricket community a home encounter with the world's strongest side, and Asian diaspora fans a familiar festival of rivalry inside a Games beyond the Commonwealth spotlight.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: IPL 2027 Auction Heads Back to India After Three Years Abroad
articles.excerpt: IPL chairman Arun Dhumal told PTI the mini auction is expected in mid-December on home soil, pending hotel availability during wedding season — while the controversial Impact Player rule also heads for a verdict.
articles.image_caption: IPL chairman Arun Dhumal holds the IPL trophy during a league event. Dhumal has confirmed the league is pushing to bring the 2027 player auction back to India after three overseas editions.
articles.nri_angle: The auction's return to Indian soil brings the IPL's signature off-field event back to diaspora fans who follow the bidding through Indian broadcasts and holiday-season watch parties, reinforcing the league's homecoming pull for NRIs traveling home in December.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: BCCI Names India ODI, T20I Squads for West Indies; Rohit Retains Place
articles.excerpt: Shubman Gill will captain a 15-man ODI squad for the three-match home series starting September 27, with Rohit Sharma and Virat Kohli retained, Dhruv Jurel preferred over Rishabh Pant as the second wicketkeeper, and Shreyas Iyer set to lead the T20I side.
articles.nri_angle: The squad shapes India's buildup to the 2027 World Cup, a campaign millions of Indian-origin fans will follow across broadcast and streaming, while the inclusion of 15-year-old Vaibhav Sooryavanshi shows how young the talent pipeline runs.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Messi to Get Buenos Aires Farewell in Final Argentina Appearance on Oct. 6
articles.excerpt: Named to Lionel Scaloni's squad despite retiring from international football on Aug. 31, Messi will play only the Oct. 6 friendly against Benin at the Estadio Monumental — his 208th cap and official send-off before Argentina's home fans.
articles.image_caption: Lionel Messi, who will play his final Argentina match at Buenos Aires' Estadio Monumental on October 6 against Benin.
articles.nri_angle: Messi's retirement lands hardest in Kerala and Kolkata, home to some of the world's most devoted Messi fanbases — from Kerala's ubiquitous giant cutouts to Kolkata's Messi-themed cafe — and for many Indian fans the Oct. 6 farewell is the proper goodbye they never got after the chaotic 2024 GOAT Tour stop.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Abhishek Sharma Rises to No. 2 as Bumrah Cracks ICC T20I Top 10
articles.excerpt: India's home series win over Afghanistan powered rankings gains across the board, with Varun Chakravarthy also climbing to fifth among T20I bowlers.
articles.image_caption: Jasprit Bumrah has broken into the top 10 of the ICC T20I bowling rankings as Abhishek Sharma rose to No. 2 among batters.
articles.nri_angle: Indian batters and bowlers dominating the T20I rankings is exactly the kind of home-nation sporting success that diaspora fans follow closely and celebrate.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: WPL Season 5 Auction Set for October 28 in Kochi, BCCI Confirms
articles.excerpt: The Board of Control for Cricket in India announced the fifth edition of the Women's Premier League will run from January 14 to February 7, 2027, with the player auction at the Grand Hyatt Kochi and a September 28 deadline for franchises to submit retention lists.
articles.image_caption: Royal Challengers Bengaluru players celebrate with the Women's Premier League trophy. The two-time champions are one of five franchises preparing for the season-five auction in Kochi on October 28.
articles.nri_angle: The WPL's mix of international stars and emerging Indian talent draws a global diaspora audience, and the October 28 Kochi auction will set the storylines NRI cricket fans in the US, UK and Australia follow through the 2027 season.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Rashid Khan Blames Shot Selection as India Close In on T20I Clean Sweep
articles.excerpt: After Afghanistan lost the second T20I by seven wickets in Delhi to hand India the series, Rashid Khan admitted his side misread the conditions and batted poorly, while BCCI vice-president Rajiv Shukla predicted a clean sweep in Thursday's final match at the Arun Jaitley Stadium.
articles.image_caption: Afghanistan players celebrate a wicket during the T20I series against India. Captain Rashid Khan took 3-36 in the second match in Delhi, where the visitors lost by seven wickets to hand India the series.
articles.nri_angle: The series, hosted in India with Afghanistan playing in front of Indian crowds, is closely followed by Afghan diaspora fans in the US and Europe and by Indian diaspora audiences whose IPL ties to Afghan stars like Rashid Khan and Mohammad Nabi add a personal thread to the fixture.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk
